description: The false-negative guard for src.generation.blanking.carrier_validation (TODO.md carrier-validation audit, 2026-08-20). Every record is a model-written carrier a previous audit cycle (docs/audits/cycle-03-report.md through cycle-09-report.md) hand-confirmed was bad German (or contained a nonsense word), quoted or reconstructed from that report. This is NOT the same fixture as data/fixtures/verification/blanking_model_verifier_adversarial.jsonl: that one measures the LLM verifier's recall; this one pins src.generation.blanking.carrier_validation.validate_carrier's own behaviour so a loosened check can never silently re-admit one of these. Two outcomes are recorded: 'rejected' (validate_carrier must keep rejecting it, with the given reason) and 'accepted' (a documented, pre-existing known miss -- carrier_validation does not catch this class today, and this record pins that its status does not change, not that the sentence is endorsed as correct German).
instructions: Golden fixture (CLAUDE.md section 7): versioned, not regenerated casually. A loosening that flips any 'rejected' record to accepted is wrong and must be reverted. Append, never edit or remove, when a future audit hand-confirms a new bad carrier.

sentence: Auf dem Weg kauft ich im Supermarkt frisches Gemüse und Milch ein.
Auf dem Boden lagen viele nassen Blätter, die ich heute Morgen sofort wegfegte.
defect: 'viele' is a plural quantifier and takes strong adjective endings ('nasse'), not the weak/mixed '-en' of 'nassen'.

sentence: Sie haben Ihren Mitreisenden ein Souvenir geschenkt, dass Sie auf dem Markt gekauft hatten.
defect: 'dass' written where the relative pronoun 'das' belongs: 'gekauft' has no accusative object, the gap the missing relative pronoun leaves behind.

sentence: Nach der Arbeit treue ich mich mit Lisa auf einen Kaffee in der Stadt.
defect: 'treue' is not a verb (the model meant 'treffe'); de_core_news_sm mistags it as a finite verb whose 1st-singular-present morphology happens to agree with 'ich', and 'treuen' collides with a real dictionary entry (an inflection of the adjective 'treu'), so no check in this module can tell it apart from a real verb lemma. Documented as a known, permanent gap in the module docstring (section 9) and pinned by its own existing unit test (test_validate_carrier_treue_hole_remains_a_documented_gap).

sentence: Der Computer ist jetzt wieder repariert, weil der Hausmeister ihn gestern schnell heilgemacht hat.
defect: 'heilgemacht' ('heil' + 'gemacht' fused as if it were one separable-verb participle) is not standard German; the intended word is 'repariert' or similar. The blanked slot itself (the Zustandspassiv) is genuinely correct German -- the fault is elsewhere in the same carrier.

sentence: Schliesslich hatte ich mich auf meinen festen Platz gesetzt, bevor der Film begann.
defect: Swiss orthography: standard German is 'Schließlich', not 'Schliesslich'.

sentence: Gleich danach war ich noch einmal kurz nach draussen gegangen, um frische Luft zu schnappen.
defect: Swiss orthography: standard German is 'draußen', not 'draussen'.

sentence: Ich wünsche mir, dass Stefan bald den Tennisschlüssel findet, den wir gestern im Park gesucht haben.
defect: 'Tennisschlüssel' ('tennis key') is not a real word; 'Tennisschläger' (tennis racket) was clearly meant. Both halves of the compound ('Tennis', 'Schlüssel') are individually real German words, so no dictionary or compound-split check can reject it -- this is a semantic-coherence defect, explicitly out of this module's scope (module docstring: 'Semantic incoherence ... is explicitly out of scope'). Caught only by the LLM verifier's own question 3, never by carrier_validation. Included here as a documented known miss, per the task's own instruction, so this boundary is pinned rather than silently assumed.
